title.en: Photosynthetic pigments and the light reaction

heading.en: How many colours are hiding in a leaf?

hook.en: A leaf looks simply green, but paper chromatography separates its extract into four bands of different colours. Each pigment catches a different part of sunlight.
hook.kn: ಎಲೆ ಕೇವಲ ಹಸಿರಾಗಿ ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದರೆ ಕಾಗದ ವರ್ಣಲೇಖನ ಅದರ ಸಾರವನ್ನು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಬಣ್ಣದ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳಾಗಿ ಬೇರ್ಪಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಣಕ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ಬೇರೆ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Name the four leaf pigments and their colours.
Relate the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a to the action spectrum.
Describe light-harvesting complexes and the two photosystems.

narration.en: A leaf looks simply green, but paper chromatography separates its extract into four bands of different colours. Each pigment catches a different part of sunlight.
narration.kn: ಎಲೆ ಕೇವಲ ಹಸಿರಾಗಿ ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದರೆ ಕಾಗದ ವರ್ಣಲೇಖನ ಅದರ ಸಾರವನ್ನು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಬಣ್ಣದ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳಾಗಿ ಬೇರ್ಪಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ವರ್ಣಕ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ಬೇರೆ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Paper chromatography of leaf pigments shows chlorophyll a (bright or blue-green), chlorophyll b (yellow-green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment of photosynthesis. Its absorption spectrum shows peaks in the blue and red regions, where the rate of photosynthesis is also highest, so the action spectrum roughly matches the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a. Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are accessory pigments: they absorb light, pass the energy to chlorophyll a, widen the range of wavelengths used, and protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.

points.en: Accessory pigments widen the useful light range and protect chlorophyll a.
Peaks of activity: blue and red light.

Its absorption spectrum shows peaks in the blue and red regions, where the rate of photosynthesis is also highest, so the action spectrum roughly matches the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a. narration.kn: ಎಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪತ್ರಹರಿತ್ತು a (ನೀಲಿ-ಹಸಿರು), ಪತ್ರಹರಿತ್ತು b (ಹಳದಿ-ಹಸಿರು), ಕ್ಸ್ಯಾಂಥೋಫಿಲ್ (ಹಳದಿ) ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ಯಾರೊಟಿನಾಯ್ಡ್ (ಹಳದಿ-ಕಿತ್ತಳೆ) ಇವೆ. ಪತ್ರಹರಿತ್ತು a ಮುಖ್ಯ ವರ್ಣಕ; ಉಳಿದವು ಸಹಾಯಕ ವರ್ಣಕಗಳು.

body.en: The light reactions (the photochemical phase) include light absorption, water splitting, oxygen release, and the formation of high-energy chemical intermediates, ATP and NADPH. Pigments are organised into two discrete photochemical light-harvesting complexes (LHC) within photosystem I (PS I) and photosystem II (PS II). Each LHC is made of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins, forming antennae; the reaction centre is a single chlorophyll a molecule. In PS I the reaction centre has an absorption peak at 700 nm (P700); in PS II at 680 nm (P680). The photosystems are named in the order of their discovery, not the order in which they work.

points.en: LHC = antenna of hundreds of pigment molecules.
PS I: P700; PS II: P680.
Reaction centre: one chlorophyll a molecule.

aim.en: Separate the pigments of a green leaf by paper chromatography and find their Rf values.

narration.en: Virtual lab. Aim: Separate the pigments of a green leaf by paper chromatography and find their Rf values.

problem.en: On a chromatogram the solvent front moved 10.0 cm and a yellow band moved 9.5 cm, a blue-green band 4.5 cm. Find the Rf values. Which band is chlorophyll a?

steps.en: Rf = distance moved by the pigment ÷ distance moved by the solvent front.
Chlorophyll a is the blue-green pigment, so the band with Rf 0.45 is chlorophyll a.
